# Project Description

We are interested in incorporating typing dynamics into our password based security system. See the included paper for additional background on this type of biometric research. In prior work (namely last semester) it was noted that a user’s typing dynamics change over time when they type a given passcode. We need to incorporate this information into the biometric system by finding a lower threshold (in terms of the number of times a person has typed a passcode in the past) with which we can start training the system.

For this project you are given access to a group of 51 individuals who have typed a passcode for a specific system.

The passcode used by this code is : \(.tie5Roanl\)

Dr. Roy Maxian and colleagues recruited 51 subjects at CMU. Subjects completed 8 data collection sessions, with each session composed of 50 times of typing the above passcode. Each session was one day apart. There is additional details concerning the data collection in the included paper.

FOR EACH SUBJECT, YOUR TASK IS TO FIND A SUBSET OF THEIR TYPING DATA THAT IS REPRESENTIVIE OF THE LEARNED TYPING BEHAVIOR.

This problem is going to be broken into the 4 following data analysis components or tasks.

[Sub-Task 1:] Develop a covariate that tells you the number of times a subject has typed the passcode in the past.

[Sub-Task 2:] For each subject, build three appropriate regression models for the total UD, total DD, and total H times in terms of the number of times the passcode has been typed.

[Sub-Task 3:] Use FDR’s to assess reasonableness of the normality assumptions of the residuals after fitting model for all subjects.

[Sub-Task 4:] Draw conclusions and make recommendations based on your analysis.

The results of your analysis should be presented in a short white paper and 15 to 30 minute powerpoint slide deck and presentation scheduled during the first week of February.



# Task-1: Covariate development

```{r}
# Loading the passcode dataset
Password_data <- read.csv("DSL-StrongPasswordData.csv", header = TRUE)
head(Password_data)
```


```{r}
#Creating a variable that counts total number of times a passcode has been typed by a subject and calculating the total time needed for hold, up-dwon and down-down time for each subject

library(dplyr)
Total_attempts <- Password_data |> 
  group_by(subject) |>  # Group data by subject
  mutate(typing_count = row_number(), # Create a new variable counting typing attempts
         total_h_time = rowSums(across(starts_with("H."))), # Create total hold time
         total_ud_time = rowSums(across(starts_with("UD."))), # Create totatl up-down time
         total_dd_time = rowSums(across(starts_with("DD.")))) |> # Create totatl down-down time
  ungroup()  # Ungroup
```

# Task-2: Building Regression Model

##To build regression model we filtered the data and considered only the top twenty password typings of each subject for each session


```{r}
# Regression models for each subject to create variable that can be view as the amount of time needed to up, down and holding the keys to type the passcode
# We used linear models
models <- model_data |>
  nest() |> # Nesting the data
  mutate(
    UD_model = map( # Fitting the linear model for up-down
      data, # Subject are second level variable
      ~ lm(total_ud_time ~ typing_count + sessionIndex, data = .x)), 
    DD_model = map( # Fitting the linear model for down-down time
      data, # Subject are second level variable
      ~ lm(total_dd_time ~ typing_count + sessionIndex, data = .x)),
    H_model = map( # Fitting the linear model for Holding
      data, # Subject are second level variable
      ~ lm(total_h_time ~ typing_count + sessionIndex, data = .x))) |>
 mutate(
    UD_model_summary = map(UD_model, summary),  # Get summary of UD_model
    DD_model_summary = map(DD_model, summary),  # Get summary of DD_model
    H_model_summary = map(H_model, summary)    # Get summary of H_model
  )

# Print the summaries
cat("Summary for UD model:\n")
models$UD_model_summary
cat("Summary for DD model:\n")
models$DD_model_summary
cat("Summary for H model:\n")
models$H_model_summary
```



# Task-3: Normality assesment

```{r}
# Define the subjects of interest
selected_subjects <- c("s002", "s020", "s040", "s057")

# Ensure 'subject' exists before filtering
if (!"subject" %in% colnames(Total_attempts)) {
  stop("Error: 'subject' column not found in Total_attempts.")
}

# Filter model_data for selected subjects
model_data <- Total_attempts |> 
  filter(subject %in% selected_subjects, rep >= 31)  # Keep only relevant subjects

# Fit models individually for each subject
filtered_models <- model_data %>%
  group_by(subject) %>%  
  nest() %>%
  mutate(
    UD_model = map(data, ~ lm(total_ud_time ~ typing_count + sessionIndex, data = .x)),  # Fit UD model
    UD_residuals = map(UD_model, residuals),  # Extract UD residuals
    UD_fitted = map(UD_model, fitted.values),  # Extract UD fitted values
  DD_model = map(data, ~ lm(total_dd_time ~ typing_count + sessionIndex, data = .x)),  # Fit DD model
    DD_residuals = map(DD_model, residuals),  # Extract DD residuals
    DD_fitted = map(DD_model, fitted.values),  # Extract DD fitted values
  H_model = map(data, ~ lm(total_h_time ~ typing_count + sessionIndex, data = .x)),  # Fit H model
    H_residuals = map(H_model, residuals),  # Extract H residuals
    H_fitted = map(H_model, fitted.values),  # Extract H fitted values
    )
```

#QQ plot for UD model
```{r}
# Load necessary libraries
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(purrr)

# Open a plotting window with 4 panels (2x2)
par(mfrow = c(2, 2), bg = "white", mar = c(4, 4, 2, 1))

# Loop through each selected subject to create QQ plots
for (subject in selected_subjects) {
  
  # Extract residuals for the current subject
  residuals_UD <- unlist(filtered_models$UD_residuals[filtered_models$subject == subject])
  
  # Create QQ plot
  qqnorm(residuals_UD,  
         main = paste("QQ Plot for UD Model (", subject, ")", sep = ""),
         xlab = "Theoretical Quantiles", ylab = "Sample Quantiles", 
         pch = 1, cex = 0.6)  # Hollow circles with smaller size
  
  # Add a reference QQ line
  qqline(residuals_UD, col = "red")
}

# Reset plotting window
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```

#Shapiro-Wilk Test for Normality Distribution
```{r}
# Perform Shapiro-Wilk test for UD, DD, and H models

# Function to perform Shapiro-Wilk test for residuals
perform_shapiro_test <- function(model_residuals, model_name, subject) {
  shapiro_test <- shapiro.test(model_residuals)
  return(data.frame(Subject = subject, Model = model_name, Statistic = shapiro_test$statistic, p_value = shapiro_test$p.value))
}

# UD Model - Shapiro-Wilk Test
shapiro_results_UD <- lapply(selected_subjects, function(subject) {
  residuals_UD <- unlist(filtered_models$UD_residuals[filtered_models$subject == subject])
  perform_shapiro_test(residuals_UD, "UD", subject)
})

# DD Model - Shapiro-Wilk Test
shapiro_results_DD <- lapply(selected_subjects, function(subject) {
  residuals_DD <- unlist(filtered_models$DD_residuals[filtered_models$subject == subject])
  perform_shapiro_test(residuals_DD, "DD", subject)
})

# H Model - Shapiro-Wilk Test
shapiro_results_H <- lapply(selected_subjects, function(subject) {
  residuals_H <- unlist(filtered_models$H_residuals[filtered_models$subject == subject])
  perform_shapiro_test(residuals_H, "H", subject)
})

# Combine all Shapiro-Wilk results into one data frame
shapiro_results_all_df <- do.call(rbind, c(shapiro_results_UD, shapiro_results_DD, shapiro_results_H))

# View the Shapiro-Wilk test results for all models
print(shapiro_results_all_df)
```


#False-Discovery Rate (FDR) - Benjamin-Hochberg
```{r}
# Apply FDR correction to the p-values using p.adjust() with method = "fdr"
shapiro_results_all_df$fdr_adjusted_p_value <- p.adjust(shapiro_results_all_df$p_value, method = "fdr")

# View the updated results with FDR adjusted p-values
print(shapiro_results_all_df)
```


```{r}
# Apply log transformation to UD and DD times (adding 1 to avoid log(0))
Total_attemptsl <- Total_attempts %>%
  mutate(
    log_total_ud_time = log(total_ud_time + 1),
    log_total_dd_time = log(total_dd_time + 1)
  )

```

```{r}
# Load necessary libraries
library(dplyr)
library(purrr)

# Re-run regression models using log-transformed UD and DD times
log_models <- Total_attemptsl %>%
  group_by(subject) %>%
  nest() %>%
  mutate(
    log_UD_model = map(data, ~ lm(log_total_ud_time ~ typing_count + sessionIndex, data = .x)), 
    log_DD_model = map(data, ~ lm(log_total_dd_time ~ typing_count+ sessionIndex, data = .x))
  )

```

```{r}
# Function to perform Shapiro-Wilk test on residuals
perform_shapiro_test <- function(residuals, model_name, subject) {
  shapiro_test <- shapiro.test(residuals)
  return(data.frame(Subject = subject, Model = model_name, Statistic = shapiro_test$statistic, P_Value = shapiro_test$p.value))
}

# Initialize list to store results
log_shapiro_results_list <- list()

# Loop through selected subjects and perform normality tests
selected_subjects <- c("s002", "s020", "s040", "s057")

for (subject in selected_subjects) {
  
  # Extract index of the subject in log_models
  i <- which(log_models$subject == subject)
  
  # Extract residuals for log-transformed models
  residuals_log_UD <- residuals(log_models$log_UD_model[[i]])
  residuals_log_DD <- residuals(log_models$log_DD_model[[i]])
  
  # Perform Shapiro-Wilk test
  log_shapiro_results_list[[paste0(subject, "_log_UD")]] <- perform_shapiro_test(residuals_log_UD, "Log_UD", subject)
  log_shapiro_results_list[[paste0(subject, "_log_DD")]] <- perform_shapiro_test(residuals_log_DD, "Log_DD", subject)
}

# Combine results into a dataframe
log_shapiro_results_df <- do.call(rbind, log_shapiro_results_list)

# Apply FDR correction
log_shapiro_results_df$FDR_Adjusted_P_Value <- p.adjust(log_shapiro_results_df$P_Value, method = "fdr")

# View results
print(log_shapiro_results_df)

```
